title: UK CPI — October 2026 consumer price inflation (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the first print containing the electricity VAT zero-rating, 13 days after the MPR that had to forecast it
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukoctober2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release page reads 'Consumer price inflation, UK: October 2026', 'Release date: 18 November 2026 7:00am', and states 'This release is not yet published'. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-electricity-vat-zero-rate-2026-10-01, 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/uk-cpi-2026-11-18.from-uk-electricity-vat-zero-rate-2026-10-01.json (read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). The proposal's placement finding stands: this is the scoring venue for the SI 2026/987 electricity VAT zero-rate, worth 0.098pp of CPI (ONS CJXA weight 20.6065/1000 x 5/105), and it publishes 13 days AFTER the 05 November MPR that had to forecast rather than observe it. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDED, AND IT REVERSES THE SIGN OF THE HEADLINE STORY: the -0.098pp is a COUNTERFACTUAL delta, not a year-on-year base effect, and measured against October 2025 the energy block is a NET UPWARD push on the annual rate. ONS series, fetched 2026-09-09: electricity D7DT rose +2.376% m/m in Oct-2025 (189.4 -> 193.9) and gas D7DU +0.951% (147.2 -> 148.6); Ofgem's 26-Aug-2026 release puts the Oct-2026 cap at +4% to GBP 1,723 from GBP 1,663 with GAS +8% and electricity-only households 'less than 1%'. Weighting those (elec 20.6065/1000, gas 10.3002/1000) gives ENERGY +0.034pp on the annual rate versus last October, not -0.10pp. SECOND FINDING, WHICH CORRECTS A SIBLING PREMISE: uk-cpi-2026-09-16 states gas and electricity are 'flat m/m by construction' inside a cap quarter. That stopped being true in April 2026 — D7DT drifted +0.43%/month and D7DU +0.55%/month through Apr-Jun 2026 where the same months of 2025 were flat to 0.1 — because ONS runs FOUR energy item indices, two of them fixed-tariff items on a 12-month rolling average whose May-2025-to-Mar-2026 cohorts were adjusted downwards from the April 2026 compilation (ONS March 2026 bulletin, fetched). Base case for the print: 2.9-3.2% y/y, under the July-MPR ~3.2% Q4 peak. THE ATTRIBUTION RULE: at 0.098pp against a headline published to one decimal the VAT cut is smaller than one rounding step, so it is not visible in the headline at all — only in the electricity index (CPI 04.5.1). Tiered LOW: symbols: [], no rates- or sterling-keyed house playbook, and the calendar's whole symbol universe is eight US mega-caps. Its real job is attribution on a crowded 11-18 (UK CPI + UK PPI 02:00 ET -> housing starts -> TIC -> FOMC minutes -> VIX expiration, 26 tracked events within five days). Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action. Ledger: docs/research/events/uk-cpi-2026-11-18.md
